lines: Now you race someone. Nine bots, or the ghost of your best ride, and every second the board ranks the field.
Each bot rides the pack's pace, easy, medium or hard, with its own drift and swing, seeded from the map: the same race rides the same way.
The standings board lists all ten by place, each bot's gap to you in seconds, and your row in orange.
The power panel reads your place, fifth of ten, with the gaps either side: level with the rider ahead, a second clear of the one behind.
When places swap, the board reorders at most once a second, and each row slides over a hundred and fifty milliseconds. With reduced motion, it simply moves.
Race solo, and it's you against your best. With no best ride yet, the ghost rides the medium pace, a hundred and ninety watts.
The panel reads Ahead or Behind, with the ghost's gap as Best. Level with your ghost counts as ahead.
Bots and the ghost run in the browser. With the maps kept on the device, a race starts and rides without a network.
From a tablet up, the board sits beside the race. On a phone it steps aside for power and the interval.
What the tests prove: seven new behaviour specs, the pace, the ranking and the gaps in unit tests, all green, and the first bundle unchanged.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
